title: Roll back the correct optimistic approval
contract: Implement reduceApproval(state, action). State is {items:[{id,status}],pending:{[id]:{requestId,before}}}. start on an existing unlocked id backs up its status and applies action.status. Ignore another start while that id is locked. failure restores the backup; success applies action.status if provided, otherwise keeps the optimistic status. Settle only matching id/requestId and remove that pending entry. Keep other loans and pending operations intact. Ignore missing IDs and unknown events. Inputs are frozen.
hints: Store the original status together with the request token for each loan.
Only the operation that owns the lock may settle it. Removing one backup must not remove another loan’s backup.

tests.name: Rejected approval restores the exact previous status
tests.explanation: A failed optimistic change must restore its own snapshot.

tests.name: A second click cannot replace an in-flight backup
tests.explanation: A duplicate start cannot replace the original owner or snapshot.

tests.name: An unrelated failure cannot roll back a newer operation
tests.explanation: Check request identity before touching a backup.

tests.name: Settling one loan preserves another pending update
tests.explanation: Concurrency is scoped to a row, not to the entire table.

tests.name: Successful server status replaces optimistic status and unlocks
tests.explanation: The confirmed server status is authoritative.

tests.name: Ignore updates for absent records
tests.explanation: Unknown IDs must not create orphaned locks.

businessContext: An officer approves a loan. The UI turns green immediately. The backend rejects the request due to an expired session or credit policy rule, but the UI remains "APPROVED", deceiving the officer.
productionSymptom: Employees believe loans are approved and disburse funds or communicate approval to borrowers, but the core banking system still records the loan as PENDING or REJECTED.
